A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Vid-LLM. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, references, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated implementation material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 3D question answering, captioning, grounding, reconstruction, and component ablations in Tables 1–9 and Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and adds comparison results, a fusion ablation, and challenging qualitative cases.

M1.justification: Equation (6) revises the stated semantic distillation loss from cosine similarity of the feature representations to cosine similarity of their mean-pooled representations. This is a localized change to the specified objective. The CTA, reconstruction and metric-depth branches, 3D patch construction, and two-stage training framework remain intact; newly documented projections and gradient routing do not independently establish further method changes.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same reasoning datasets—ScanQA, SQA3D, Scan2Cap, ScanRefer, Multi3DRefer, Nr3D, and Sr3D—and reconstruction datasets—Co3Dv2, RealEstate10K, NYU Depth v2, and ScanNet. The additional comparisons and selected challenging cases analyze retained tasks without establishing a new dataset, population, or separately defined evaluation scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 add LLaVA-3D, Video-3D LLM, and 3DRS variants; Tables 2–3 also add VGLLM. Table 2 removes 3D-VisTA and LL3DA, while Table 3 removes 3D-VisTA and 3D-LLM. Table 5 expands to Uni3DR2 and VGLLM-Rec while reducing the separately reported concatenation variants. Tables 7–9 newly compare against VGGT. These substantially broaden and revise the comparator set.

E3.justification: The Nr3D/Sr3D protocol description changes from ViL3DRel-generated grounding candidates to provided segmentation annotations. Added comparisons introduce VGGT-generated geometry for 3DRS, ground-truth camera poses for Uni3DR2, and ground-truth scale alignment for VGGT depth and point-cloud evaluation. These revise or extend settings within retained benchmarks; the PDFs do not establish which existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Table 6 adds CTA–Concat-SA to test concatenation followed by self-attention; the previous no-bridge configuration is clarified as cross-attention. Appendix A.1 and new Figure 7 add cases examining undercounting, undersized grounding boxes, and successful captioning despite incomplete geometry. Existing bridge-token, metric-depth, and training-strategy ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. Averages across evaluation metrics are retained and do not constitute uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces Vid-LLM's ScanRefer accuracies 50.1/46.7 with 63.2/56.4 and Multi3DRefer accuracies 47.2/42.9 with 61.6/56.1. Changed protocol documentation prevents treating these as established same-setting gains. Table 2 changes BLEU-4 from 40.6 to 40.9, and numerous comparator and ablation results are added. Vid-LLM's QA, Nr3D/Sr3D, and reconstruction scores remain unchanged. In v2, Table 5 reports ScanRefer 59.8 while Table 6 retains 48.4 for the full model, without reconciling the difference.

T1.justification: Equation (6) changes the mathematical specification of semantic distillation by explicitly applying mean pooling before cosine similarity. The accompanying definitions clarify normalization and feature dimensions. The remaining mathematical framework is retained, and neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same substantive claims: video-based reconstruction and reasoning, geometry–semantics integration through CTA, metric-scale recovery, and two-stage training. Changes to comparative findings occur in the experimental discussion rather than these core contribution claims.

C2.justification: The experimental interpretation shifts from broad QA/captioning superiority toward leadership among video-based models, and from reconstruction superiority toward competitiveness with the newly included VGGT teacher. Grounding is now interpreted as outperforming the expanded comparator set. Appendix A.1 adds substantive applicability limits: incomplete geometry harms counting and grounding, whereas sufficient 2D cues can preserve captioning performance.

D1.justification: v2 adds pooling, feature-projection, and gradient-routing details, plus Mask3D proposal/segmentation and annotation-use information. Much of v1 Appendix A.3 moves into Section 4.1, retaining backbone, frame sampling, resizing, and optimizer settings. However, augmentation, FlashAttention, QK-Norm, mixed-precision, and activation-checkpointing details are omitted. Code and data access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for 3DRS, Video-3D LLM, VGLLM, and Mask3D, and briefly discusses VGLLM as a closely related video-based approach using VGGT geometry features. The broader related-work organization and positioning around geometry–semantics integration remain.

P1.justification: v2 introduces an Experimental Setup subsection using relocated implementation material, rewrites the comparison discussion around joint reconstruction–reasoning models, and expands training explanations and appendix analysis. It also standardizes CTA capitalization and adds conference headers. The overall narrative structure and most introductory and methodological text remain.

P2.justification: v2 adds the three-case Figure 7, separates 3D-based and video-based methods in Tables 2–3, and expands Table 5 with task columns and model categories. Other tables gain rows and explanatory annotations. Figures 1–6 are retained, with local resizing and relocation rather than a wholesale visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides more informative comparisons against close competitors and the VGGT teacher, clearer training/evaluation specifications, and explicit failure analysis in Figure 7. These improve assessment of the method's strengths and boundaries. The benefit is limited by omitted implementation details and the unexplained ScanRefer discrepancy between Tables 5 and 6; the higher grounding scores alone do not establish improved paper quality.
